title: Middle Schooler’s Dyslexia Podcast Wins National Contest
summary:
A seventh-grader from Long Island, New York, has won the middle-school grand prize in NPR’s Student Podcast Challenge. Cora Walsh of Rockville Centre created a podcast called “Dyslexia and MEE” about her long path to understanding why reading was so hard.

Cora has dyslexia, a learning difference that can make reading more difficult. She said it took almost five years to get the correct diagnosis. For a long time she knew only that reading felt confusing, even when she practiced more than her friends.

Her podcast was chosen from nearly 1,500 submissions from 42 states and the District of Columbia. Cora said she felt excited about the win. Her mom, Emily Johnson, said she was proud of how hard her daughter works and of her positive attitude.

Cora has received tutoring for dyslexia for two years. In the podcast, listeners hear part of a Zoom lesson where she practices sounding out words while her tutor gives feedback. She says she is a better reader now and enjoys reading more. This summer, her mom saw her pick up the first Hunger Games book for fun—on trips and even while reading to her pet rabbit.

Cora hopes the podcast will help dyslexia feel less scary for other kids who are still figuring out how they learn. She says she is proud that she kept trying and made something interesting for others to hear. She has already checked out the second Hunger Games book from the library.

Dyslexia does not mean a person cannot learn to read. With the right support, many students improve and find strategies that work for them.
why_it_matters: Winning a national student contest can spotlight learning differences and show peers that persistence and the right support matter. Stories like Cora’s help normalize dyslexia and encourage kids still seeking answers.
